note: The verifier's pins for TEE scores. Every accepted build is a canonical build: tee/build-docker.sh (Linux x86_64 in a digest-pinned Rust image), which gives the same bytes on any host with Docker, from tee/ at the commit recorded below. v2 scores the six re-scored rounds and round 4 (which sealed it); v3 adds request template v3 and scores round 5, which sealed it; v4 also counts unreadable answers in end-to-end-encrypted rounds; v5 rounds a numeric difference to 28 significant digits exactly as the sealed Python scorer's Decimal arithmetic does; v6 scores an answer that doesn't decrypt 0 even when the item accepts an empty answer; v7 scores exactly as v6 and adds the ground mode, which checks every answer key against its cited near/docs line; v8 scores exactly as v7 and adds the numeric grounding rule; v9, current, scores and grounds as v8 and adds the asked-check. Neither ever echoes a sealed value in an error. Scorer v1 (a848254b9d2cda2ca522e839b4e4f7de33ec1d51a364fb9a0d92d88f252f69a7, tee/build.sh at commit f9bbbe9, reproducible on macOS arm64 only) was retired on 2026-11-05 after all six of its scores were re-done with v2.

asker_note: An enclave-asked round (audit mode tee-asked-v1) seals one of these (build, project) pairs. The verifier also checks, at the round's seal block, that the project's owner account had no keys and no code and that the build was the project's only version, so nobody could delete the project (wiping its records) or change its code.
